title: Perimeter of Quadrilaterals and Composite Figures
seo_title: Grade 4 Perimeter Worksheets with Answers (MATATAG Math 4)
standard_text: Find the perimeter of quadrilaterals that are not squares or rectangles; find the perimeter of composite figures composed of triangles and quadrilaterals.
meta_desc: Free Grade 4 perimeter worksheets for the DepEd MATATAG curriculum: perimeter of trapezoids, parallelograms, kites and composite figures made of triangles and quadrilaterals. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Perimeter: add all the outside sides.
key_sub: Lines inside a composite figure do not count.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • The perimeter is the distance around a figure. Add the lengths of all the outside sides.
  • Equal sides help: a parallelogram has 2 pairs of equal opposite sides, a kite has 2 pairs of equal sides next to each other.
  • For a composite figure, go around the outside only. Lines inside the figure are not part of the perimeter.
  • Write the unit (cm or m) in the answer.

Examples

Example

House shape: square sides 10 cm, roof sides 7 cm

Outside: 7 + 7 + 10 + 10 + 10

Answer: 44 cm

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Counting an inside lineOnly the outside counts.
Leaving out a sideCount the sides before adding.
Multiplying the sidesPerimeter is a sum; area uses multiplication.

faq.q: What does MATATAG Math 4 ask about perimeter?
faq.a: Find the perimeter of quadrilaterals that are not squares or rectangles, and find the perimeter of composite figures composed of triangles and quadrilaterals.
A unit of length, like cm or m.

faq.q: Is perimeter the same as area?
faq.a: No. Perimeter is the distance around; area is the space inside.

faq.q: How do I find a missing side?
faq.a: Subtract the known sides from the perimeter.

items.q: A rectangle has a perimeter of 30 m. It is 12 m long. How wide is it?
items.e: The two lengths use 12 + 12 = 24 m. That leaves 30 − 24 = 6 m for the two widths, so each width is 3 m.

items.q: The perimeter of this triangle is 31 cm. What is the missing side length?
items.e: Add the sides you know: 8 + 12 = 20. Then subtract from the perimeter: 31 − 20 = 11 cm.

items.q: The perimeter of this quadrilateral is 21 cm. What is the missing side length?

items.q: A square has a perimeter of 12 m. How long is each side?

items.q: The perimeter of this triangle is 26 m. What is the missing side length?

items.q: A square sandbox has a perimeter of 20 m. How long is each side?

items.q: A chessboard has 8 rows of 8 squares. How many squares are there on the board?
items.e: 8 rows of 8 squares: 8 × 8 = 64 squares. (32 is the number of square sides around the edge.)

items.q: The school playground is a rectangle 30 m long and 20 m wide. How far is it once around the edge?
items.e: Once round is the perimeter: 30 + 20 + 30 + 20 = 100 m.

items.q: A rectangular vegetable patch is 12 m long and 8 m wide. A fence goes all the way around, except for a gate that is 2 m wide. How much fence is needed?
items.e: Perimeter: 12 + 8 + 12 + 8 = 40 m. There is no fence across the gate: 40 − 2 = 38 m.

items.q: A patio is made of square paving slabs. Each slab is 1 m by 1 m. There are 5 rows of 4 slabs. What is the area of the patio?
items.e: Count the slabs: 5 rows of 4 is 5 × 4 = 20 slabs, so the area is 20 square meters.

items.q: Kenneth’s family puts a fence around their rectangular garden. The garden is 14 m long and 9 m wide. How much fence do they need?
items.e: The fence goes along all 4 sides: 14 + 9 + 14 + 9 = 46 m.

items.q: A rectangular flower bed has a perimeter of 30 m. One side is 9 m long. How long is the side next to it?
items.e: The two 9 m sides make 18 m. 30 − 18 = 12 m for the other two sides, so each is 12 ÷ 2 = 6 m. Check: 9 + 6 + 9 + 6 = 30 m.

items.q: In PE, Arnel runs around a rectangular field 2 times. The field is 25 m long and 15 m wide. How far does he run?
items.e: Once round: 25 + 15 + 25 + 15 = 80 m. Two times round: 2 × 80 = 160 m.

items.q: Paolo has 1 m of ribbon. He puts ribbon around the edge of a card that is 20 cm by 12 cm. How much ribbon is left?
items.e: 1 m = 100 cm. Perimeter of the card: 20 + 12 + 20 + 12 = 64 cm. Left: 100 − 64 = 36 cm.

items.q: Carla wants to put colored tape around the edge of a picture. What should she work out?
items.e: Tape goes around the edge, so find the perimeter. Perimeter is a length, so it is in cm.
